In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
social capital is the sum of the actual and potential resources embedded within, and derived from, network of relationships.
social capital is a set of norms, values, and institutions that facilitate cooperation and coordination among people. The idea of
social capital is about networks of relationships and the norms of reciprocity that are embedded in those networks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
social capital is not a single thing.

social capital is a set of norms and networks that facilitates coordination and cooperation for mutual benefit, and that it can be both a private and public good, and it can have both public and private returns.
social capital, in its various forms, is a public good that is not necessarily excludable but is often partially excludable and not necessarily rivalrous.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are many different types of social capital, and they have very different consequences for the people who have them and for the societies in which they live.
social capital is not just a matter of having friends, or having friends who are rich.
there is a very wide variety of social capital.
